answer: Hypothesis: The -0.9568 factor (log-odds coefficient) of BA degree completion applies between the two races Black and White — specifically, it is the coefficient for Black respondents relative to White respondents, with White as the reference category, in a logistic regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED on race with a race-by-SES interaction (BA ~ race*SES). Black respondents have significantly lower log-odds of completing a BA degree than White respondents at SES = 0 (coefficient = -0.9568, OR = 0.384, SE = 0.2154, z = -4.44, p < 0.001). So the two races are Black and White (Black vs White, Black compared with the White reference group).

payload.workflow: 1) Loaded 8773x9 nls_ses_processed.csv (no missing, no duplicates, no weights). 2) Fitted logistic regression BA DEGREE COMPLETED ~ race*SES with White as reference; Black main effect = -0.956778 ≈ -0.9568 (SE .2154, p<.001, OR .3841, 95%CI .2519-.5859). 3) Enumerated all three reference codings; only White-ref Black contrast equals -0.9568 (all other pairs: +/-0.7160, +/-0.2408, +0.9568). 4) Sensitivity: adding sex keeps it near (-0.9592) but adding ability (+0.1351), percentile (-0.7006), family size (-0.3807) or all (+0.4422) breaks the exact match, showing the match is specific to the race*SES specification. 5) Full-sample complete-case unweighted analysis delivered with reproducible script artifact.
